subtopics.title: Why Atoms Bond, and the Lewis Diagram Toolkit

questions.question: Two hydrogen atoms form a bond while two helium atoms do not because:
options: Sharing electrons lowers the hydrogen atoms' energy, while helium's filled shell gains nothing from sharing
Hydrogen atoms carry opposite charges
Helium atoms are too heavy to bond
Hydrogen atoms repel all other elements

questions.question: On the potential energy versus distance curve for two hydrogen atoms, the bond length is read at:
options: The point where the energy is zero
The steepest part of the curve
The separation where the energy curve reaches its minimum
The largest separation plotted

questions.question: In the Lewis diagram of water, oxygen carries:
options: Four bonding pairs and no lone pairs
Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs
One bonding pair and three lone pairs
Three bonding pairs and one lone pair

questions.question: A dative covalent bond, as in the ammonium ion, is a bond in which:
options: The electrons transfer completely to one atom
Three pairs are shared simultaneously
Each atom contributes one electron of the pair
One atom supplies both electrons of the shared pair

questions.question: Electron pairs around a central atom settle into the arrangement that:
options: Places them as far apart as possible, because they repel one another
Packs them as close together as possible
Matches the flat drawing in the workbook
Minimises the size of the molecule

questions.question: Methane, with four bonding pairs, has the shape of a:
options: Flat square with 90° angles
Trigonal pyramid
Tetrahedron with 109,5° angles
Linear chain

questions.question: Water has four electron pairs around its oxygen, yet its shape is called angular because:
options: Oxygen rejects the tetrahedral arrangement
Its bonds are double bonds
The hydrogen atoms push each other into a line
Shapes are named from the atoms only, and two of the four pairs are lone pairs

questions.question: The bond angle shrinks from 109,5° in methane to about 104,5° in water because:
options: Water's bonds are longer
Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs and squeeze the bonds together
Oxygen is heavier than carbon
Water contains fewer electrons

subtopics.title: Electronegativity and the Polarity of Bonds

questions.question: Electronegativity is defined as:
options: The number of valence electrons on an atom
The energy released when a bond forms
A measure of an atom's tendency to attract the shared electron pair in a bond
The charge carried by an ion

questions.question: In hydrogen fluoride (H: 2,1; F: 4,0), the fluorine end of the bond is:
options: δ−, because fluorine attracts the shared pair more strongly
δ+, because fluorine is smaller
Neutral
Fully ionised

questions.question: A bond between two identical atoms, such as Cl–Cl, is always:
options: Ionic
Polar covalent
Dative
Non-polar covalent, because the electronegativity difference is zero

questions.question: Sodium chloride (Na: 0,9; Cl: 3,0) is classified as ionic because:
options: Its crystals are large
The electronegativity difference of 2,1 is large enough for essentially complete electron transfer
Sodium attracts the shared pair strongly
Chlorine donates its electrons to sodium

subtopics.title: Polar Molecules, Bond Energy and Bond Length

questions.question: Carbon dioxide contains two polar bonds yet is a non-polar molecule because:
options: Carbon and oxygen have equal electronegativities
Its bonds are secretly non-polar
Its linear shape points the two equal bond dipoles in exactly opposite directions, cancelling them
The molecule spins too fast to be polar

questions.question: Water IS a polar molecule because:
options: Its angular shape stops its two bond dipoles from cancelling
It contains two hydrogen atoms
Its bonds are stronger than most
Oxygen is a heavy atom

questions.question: Comparing carbon-carbon single, double and triple bonds:
options: The single bond is the strongest
All three are the same length
The double bond is the shortest
The triple bond is the shortest and strongest

questions.question: Descending a group of the periodic table, bonds from those atoms to hydrogen generally become:
options: Shorter and stronger
Longer and weaker, because larger atoms bond at greater distances
Shorter and weaker
Longer and stronger

questions.question: In the energy-hollow picture, atoms bond because:
options: Settling into the hollow lowers their energy
The hollow heats them up
Higher energy means more stability
They are attracted to larger atoms

questions.question: The depth of the energy hollow represents:
options: The bond length
The number of lone pairs
The bond energy — how much work it takes to pull the atoms apart
The size of the atoms

questions.question: In a Lewis diagram, a lone pair is drawn as:
options: A pair of dots between two atoms
A pair of dots resting on its own atom, shared with nobody
A line joining three atoms
A single dot outside the molecule

questions.question: Four balloons knotted at their necks spring into a tetrahedron because:
options: The knot forces that angle
Balloons always sink into pyramids
Air pressure squeezes them together
Each balloon shoves the others as far away as it can

questions.question: Ammonia is called pyramidal rather than tetrahedral because:
options: One of its four electron pairs is a lone pair, and shapes are named from visible atoms only
It has only three electron pairs in total
Its bonds are all double bonds
Nitrogen refuses tetrahedral geometry

questions.question: The flat cross drawn for methane in a workbook is:
options: Methane's true geometry
Correct only for cold methane
A two-dimensional shadow of the real tetrahedral shape
Wrong — methane is trigonal planar

questions.question: In the tug-of-war picture, electronegativity is:
options: The thickness of the rope
Each atom's pulling strength on the shared electrons
The referee's whistle
The length of the contest

questions.question: The change from covalent to ionic bonding is best described as:
options: A smooth slide from fair sharing through unfair sharing to outright taking, positioned by the electronegativity difference
A sharp wall at a difference of exactly 2,0
Two unrelated kinds of chemistry
Something that only happens in solution

questions.question: A molecule containing polar bonds is nevertheless non-polar overall when:
options: It contains an even number of atoms
Its bonds are all single bonds
It is warmed above room temperature
Its shape makes the bond pulls cancel exactly, as in linear carbon dioxide

questions.question: Water's bent shape matters because it:
options: Makes the molecule easier to freeze
Cancels the pulls of the two hydrogens
Stops the two bond pulls from cancelling, leaving the whole molecule polar
Lets the molecule stack into crystals
